articles.originalTitle: Frieze London 2026 - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Frieze London 2026 Art Fair Opens With a Greater Focus on the Global South
articles.excerpt: The 2026 editions of Frieze London and Frieze Masters feature increased representation from the Global South, alongside new awards, specialized curatorial threads, and contemporary art market discussions.
articles.content: The 2026 edition of Frieze London and Frieze Masters reflects a shifting balance towards the Global South, featuring increased non-Western art alongside galleries from North Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia. Alongside the fair activities, ongoing industry developments such as the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR) requiring sustainability reports from galleries and museums, and the ongoing university staff strike at Goldsmiths, have drawn significant attention. During the London events, Okiki Akinfe won the inaugural £30,000 emerging artist prize supported by the Dasha Shenkman Focus Fund. Specialized exhibitions at Frieze Masters introduced modernist works through a queer lens, highlighting contributions from international LGBTQ+ artists. Additionally, a new Abu Dhabi cultural district named Noma was announced ahead of the emirate's inaugural Frieze fair. Galleries offering radical works adapted successfully to changing buying patterns during the week.

articles.originalTitle: Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography Exhibition Guide - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern Exhibition Explores the Pictorialism Art Photography Movement
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern presents over 200 rare vintage prints focusing on pictorialism, an international movement asserting photography as a genuine art form.
articles.content: Tate Modern is hosting an exhibition titled "Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography," exploring pictorialism, the first international art photography movement that established photography as an expressive art form. Running from October 14, 2026, to February 21, 2027, the exhibition features over 200 rare vintage photographic prints from around the world. Originating in the 1880s, pictorialist photographers experimented with darkroom chemistry, negative manipulation, and diverse papers, borrowing compositions and moods from painting. A working darkroom is integrated into the exhibition space, allowing visitors on select days to create prints using vintage and environmentally friendly techniques. The presentation highlights works by figures such as Alvin Langdon Coburn, Lionel Wendt, Cavendish Morton, and Soichi Sunami, spanning portraiture, collaborations with modern dancers, and alternative analogue printing processes like platinum and bromoil prints. Furthermore, the exhibition extends beyond Europe and the United States to showcase the modernist aesthetic contributions of groups such as Brazil's Foto Cine Clube Bandeirante.

articles.originalTitle: Anatomy and Astronomy in the National Art Library - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: National Art Library Highlights Early Medical and Astronomical Textbooks
articles.excerpt: The National Art Library at the Victoria and Albert Museum houses rare early textbooks focusing on human anatomy and astronomy.
articles.content: The National Art Library within the Victoria and Albert Museum maintains rare early volumes on human anatomy and astronomy among its collections. Notable items include Andreas Vesalius's volume commonly known as De humani corporis fabrica libri septem, widely regarded as the first accurate anatomical textbook. Working during the Italian Renaissance, the Padua professor collaborated with German artist Jan Steven van Calcar to produce over 250 woodcut illustrations detailing internal human structures. Another scientific volume held in the library is the 1799 second edition of A compendious system of astronomy by Margaret Bryan, a school founder who compiled her lectures on planetary distances and motions for students. The publication refers to Uranus by the historical designation Georgium Sidus, a name utilized for decades following the planet's discovery. These volumes form part of the institution's Clements Collection and are accessible for viewing by appointment within the special collections reading rooms after standard registration.

articles.originalTitle: Designing with Multifunctional Metal Systems - Architectural Record
articles.title: Design Role of Multifunctional Metal Systems in Hunters View Project
articles.excerpt: The multifunctional aluminum sunshades and large-scale wallscreen used in San Francisco's Hunters View residential project demonstrate how envelope design and installation efficiency can be optimized under tight budgets and schedules.
articles.content: In San Francisco's Bayview neighborhood, Hunters View Blocks 14 and 17—a 118-unit LEED Gold affordable housing community designed by David Baker Architects—implemented multifunctional envelope systems. Provided by metal fabricator BŌK Modern, custom anodized aluminum Simple Mount sunshades deliver solar control at windows, while a large-scale wallscreen gives the two-building composition a shared visual identity. Developed by David Baker Architects, the semi-randomized circle-based grid creates dynamic shadows that shift with viewing distance and time of day. Designed with a direct-mount attachment approach, the sunshades eliminated protruding brackets, reduced site mobilizations, and achieved installation costs up to 33 percent lower than conventional systems. Manufactured in California with recycled content, the aluminum systems help reduce cooling loads and support the building's LEED Gold certification. Project stakeholders resolved performance and design intent prior to fabrication through early coordination programs.

articles.originalTitle: Thin concrete plane defines minimalist villa in Ibiza by Fran Silvestre Arquitectos - Dezeen
articles.title: Fran Silvestre Arquitectos Completes Minimalist Ibiza Villa with Thin Concrete Plane
articles.excerpt: Spanish studio Fran Silvestre Arquitectos has completed Bellavista 11, a minimalist villa on an Ibiza hillside shaped by a 15-centimetre-thick white concrete plane.
articles.content: Spanish studio Fran Silvestre Arquitectos has completed Bellavista 11, the first villa in The Roca Views development in Roca Lisa on Ibiza's eastern coast. Designed as a contemporary interpretation of the island's traditional white-walled buildings, the project centers on a single continuous element that follows the local topography. Studio founder Fran Silvestre explained that the design adapts to the slope while organizing the interior program and orienting rooms toward the landscape. Defined by a white concrete plane measuring just 15 centimetres thick, the villa steps down the hillside across three low-slung volumes. The layout begins with a garage and access stair, moves through a central social area, and concludes with a five-bedroom block. Interiors feature white walls, pale stone floors, and timber carpentry designed to emphasize the shifting daylight. The open-plan living, dining, and kitchen space connects to a swimming pool, while full-height sliding glass doors with slender frames provide access to the terraces. Photography for the project was provided by Jesus Orrico.

articles.originalTitle: Generative: A Computer Art Documentary - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum to Screen Computer Art Documentary
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum will host a special screening of the documentary Generative, exploring early experiments with code, chance, and machines, followed by a Q&A.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum will present a special cut of the documentary film Generative, exploring the integration of computers into creative processes. The screening is scheduled for 7 November 2026 at the Lydia and Manfred Gorvy Lecture Theatre within V&A South Kensington in London. Following the screening, a question-and-answer session will feature the film's director and producer alongside the museum's digital art curator. Through rare archives and interviews with figures such as Vera Molnar, Manfred Mohr, and A. Michael Noll, the documentary traces how artists and engineers initially brought computers into creative practices. Directed by Ben Spilling and produced by Amber Tordoff-Gibson, the film examines the enduring influence of these early experiments involving code, chance, and machines on contemporary artists. This presentation forms part of the institution's Digital Art Season, which investigates the shifting boundaries between human and machine agency. The event is free, though advance booking is required for attendees wishing to secure a seat.

articles.originalTitle: snøhetta unveils completed shanghai grand opera house with spiraling public rooftop - Designboom
articles.title: Snøhetta-Designed Shanghai Grand Opera House Opens on the Huangpu River
articles.excerpt: Spanning 146,786 square meters along the Huangpu River, the newly completed Shanghai Grand Opera House features three auditoriums and a public spiraling rooftop.
articles.content: Following nearly a decade in development, Snøhetta’s Shanghai Grand Opera House officially opened on the banks of the Huangpu River. Spanning 146,786 square meters, the completed building houses three auditoriums with a combined capacity of 4,200 seats, alongside rehearsal, production, education, exhibition, and hospitality facilities. The project originated from a winning proposal in a 2016 international competition, developed in collaboration with East China Architectural Design & Research Institute, Theatre Projects, and Nagata Acoustics. The building's defining architectural gesture is a sweeping white roof that rises from the surrounding landscape in a continuous spiral, inspired by traditional Chinese fan geometry and the Huangpu River. A sculptural staircase leads visitors to the elevated roof, transforming it into an accessible observation deck and gathering space requiring no admission ticket. Inside, the architecture transitions to richly textured performance spaces, featuring the 2,000-seat Harmony Hall with a dark-red interior for enhanced vocal acoustics, the 1,200-seat Soar Theatre, and the 1,000-seat Open Stage with adaptable seating configurations. The venue's inaugural season runs through February 20, 2027, featuring 82 performances across 47 productions.

articles.originalTitle: Ibrahim Mahama’s Most Ambitious Show Yet Is Headed to Paris—But Its Core Is in Ghana - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Ghanaian Artist Ibrahim Mahama Opens Major Exhibition at Fondation Cartier in Paris
articles.excerpt: Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama is launching his most ambitious exhibition yet at the Fondation Cartier in Paris, featuring Asante Empire royal stools and a reconstruction of the Aboso Glass Factory.
articles.content: Ghanaian artist Ibrahim Mahama is launching his new exhibition titled "The Harvest Season" at the Fondation Cartier in Paris, occupying the institution's entire building. The artist describes the show as his most ambitious project to date. The exhibition features a new iteration of his 2019 installation "Parliament of Ghosts," which incorporates discarded train seats, railway sleepers, school furniture, and jute sacks. This version includes roughly 200 restored royal stools from the Asante Empire. Mahama aims to highlight a contradiction by presenting these objects for free access rather than keeping them in museum glass cases. The exhibition also introduces a new project titled "Things Fall Apart," centered on the reconstruction of the abandoned Aboso Glass Factory, established in 1966 by Ghana's first president, Kwame Nkrumah. The factory reconstruction is supported by production funds from the Fondation Cartier and will eventually return to Ghana for permanent installation. In addition, the show displays works regarding the Ganaian railway system and a new textile installation hung across the facades of the building, created in collaboration with various artists and collectives.

articles.originalTitle: New Abu Dhabi cultural district announced ahead of the emirate’s inaugural Frieze fair - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: New Abu Dhabi cultural district announced ahead of inaugural Frieze fair
articles.excerpt: Abu Dhabi has announced Noma, a new creative neighbourhood developed by Aldar, ahead of the emirate's inaugural Frieze fair in the Saadiyat Cultural District. The upcoming event will feature 88 galleries with a strong focus on the SWANA region.
articles.content: Weeks ahead of the inaugural Frieze fair in the United Arab Emirates, Abu Dhabi has unveiled a new creative neighbourhood named Noma. Announced on Thursday by Aldar, the leading real-estate developer and official fair partner, the district derives its name from its location north of Manarat Al Saadiyat. The inaugural Frieze Abu Dhabi is scheduled to run from 19 to 22 November within the Saadiyat Cultural District, which already hosts the Louvre Abu Dhabi, Zayed National Museum, and the Guggenheim Abu Dhabi, set to open in December. The upcoming fair will bring together 88 galleries with a primary focus on the SWANA region, alongside public sculpture installations along the Mamsha coastline and a Frieze Masters section curated by Marika Sardar. While recent geopolitical tensions and airspace closures in the region have caused concern among some gallerists, the fair organisers and the Department of Culture and Tourism have confirmed that preparations for the 19 November opening are well advanced and that they will offer travel flexibility to affected participants.

articles.originalTitle: Meet the collectors | Laurent Dumas - Art Basel
articles.title: New Contemporary Art Center Le Large Opens Near Paris
articles.excerpt: Founded by Emerige real estate group CEO Laurent Dumas, Le Large opens its doors in Boulogne-Billancourt, welcoming visitors with its inaugural exhibition titled 'Moteur Imaginaire'.
articles.content: Located on the western edge of Greater Paris in Boulogne-Billancourt, the new contemporary art center Le Large opens on October 17 and 18, 2026. Founded by Laurent Dumas, CEO of the real estate group Emerige, the center focuses on showcasing artists living and working in France. For its inaugural exhibition, titled 'Moteur Imaginaire', Le Large explores the history of Île Seguin, which served as a Renault automotive factory site for nearly a century. Italian curator Cecilia Alemani has brought together around 60 artists for the exhibition, including Neïl Beloufa, Bianca Bondi, Théo Mercier, Jean-Luc Moulène, and Laure Prouvost. The exhibition examines how the machine is evolving today, its impact on humankind, and its representation as a force for emancipation. 'Moteur Imaginaire' runs from October 17, 2026, to March 7, 2027. Additionally, Laurent Dumas will participate in a conversation with artist Eva Jospin on Thursday, October 22, 2026, as part of the Art Basel Paris 2026 Conversations program.

articles.originalTitle: Tate Modern exhibition explores Pictorialism and the birth of soft-focus photography - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Tate Modern Exhibition Explores Pictorialism and the Birth of Soft-Focus Photography
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern's new exhibition, Light and Magic, re-evaluates the global networks and enduring 20th-century influence of Pictorialism, a movement that sought to elevate photography to fine art.
articles.content: Tate Modern is presenting Light and Magic, an exhibition focusing on Pictorialism, a salon-based photography movement that sought to establish photography as a fine art on a par with painting and sculpture. Curated by Charmaine Toh, the revisionist show challenges the conventional view that the movement ended in the 1920s or remained confined to Europe and North America. Instead, it highlights works produced worldwide into the 1950s and 1960s, supported by international clubs and exhibitions. Featuring works by pioneers such as Alfred Stieglitz, Robert Demachy, and Luo Bonian, the exhibition examines how practitioners manipulated visual elements to emulate subjective forms like Impressionism and traditional ink drawings. Running until 21 February 2027, the display reclaims Pictorialism's vital position alongside Modernism in the history of 20th-century art.

articles.originalTitle: Honoring Legendary Designer Yohji Yamamoto and Artist Danh Vo - WWD
articles.title: Yohji Yamamoto and Danh Vo Honored With Isamu Noguchi Award
articles.excerpt: Designer Yohji Yamamoto and artist Danh Vo received the Isamu Noguchi Award at the Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum annual benefit.
articles.content: Fashion designer Yohji Yamamoto and contemporary artist Danh Vo received the Isamu Noguchi Award at the Isamu Noguchi Foundation and Garden Museum annual benefit. The honorees were recognized for their multidisciplinary practices and artistic integrity. Museum director Amy Hau presented the award, noting Danh Vo's artistic engagement with themes of migration, colonialism, and identity. Yohji Yamamoto, who could not attend, was honored through a special film reflecting on Isamu Noguchi's artistic language bridging East and West. Yamamoto is recognized for challenging conventional ideas of fashion, proportion, and silhouette over a career spanning more than five decades. The annual benefit serves as the museum's primary fundraising event to support its exhibitions, educational programs, and the preservation of Noguchi's archives. The gathering also marked the 75th anniversary of Noguchi's Akari light sculptures.

articles.originalTitle: Art Week NYC Announces Participating Institutions for Inaugural Event - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Art Week NYC Announces Participating Institutions for Inaugural Event
articles.excerpt: Scheduled for November 11 through 14, the inaugural Art Week NYC has announced a list of 32 participating institutions, including the Whitney Museum and the Queens Museum.
articles.content: Taking place across the city from November 11 through 14, the four-day inaugural Art Week NYC has announced a list of 32 participating institutions. The event includes museums such as the Whitney Museum of American Art, the Studio Museum in Harlem, and the Queens Museum, alongside nonprofits like ArtTable and the Madison Square Park Conservancy. Launched this summer by ARTnews, Art in America, and Artforum, the organization aims to bring together galleries, museums, and audiences over four days of programming, from walking tours to gallery openings. The event centers around four main gallery neighborhoods: Chelsea, the Lower East Side, Tribeca, and the Upper East Side. City Council Speaker Julie Menin stated that the week opens the door for local artists and art lovers to support creative institutions. On Saturday, November 14, public programming will take place at the New Museum, the main institutional partner. Artforum's series of five talks titled 'Art and the City' will feature conversations on topics including the redesign of museum spaces, the movement of artists into filmmaking, economic conditions, and machine intelligence in studio practice.

articles.originalTitle: Factory in Bangladesh that "redefines manufacturing architecture" wins RIBA International Prize - Dezeen
articles.title: Bangladesh Rug Factory Wins the 2026 RIBA International Prize
articles.excerpt: Designed by Nakshabid Architects in Rangpur, the Green Field Factory has won the 2026 RIBA International Prize for its passive design principles and focus on employee wellbeing.
articles.content: Designed by Nakshabid Architects in Rangpur, Bangladesh, the Green Field Factory has won the 2026 RIBA International Prize, awarded biennially to the world's best new building outside the UK. Commissioned by Karupannya Rangpur Limited, the seven-storey structure draws inspiration from the traditional Bengali home, incorporating natural ventilation and biophilic design principles. The building features courtyards, verandas, gardens, and a monumental green facade to minimize the need for mechanical systems. It features one main entrance with two grand staircases for all workers to challenge workplace hierarchies. The facility also includes a rooftop daycare centre, medical practice, grocery shop, and prayer room to support workers and the wider community. The RIBA jury praised the project for supporting its female workforce and redefining manufacturing architecture. The winner was announced at the Stirling Prize ceremony in London.

articles.originalTitle: Awakenings: Artists and Curator in Conversation - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Hosts a Two-Part Conversation on AI and Art
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum welcomes Aziza Kadyri and Eunjo Lee as part of the Awakenings programme, examining how digital systems and artificial intelligence shape art practices. The event takes place on 17 October 2026 at V&A South Kensington.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting a conversation series as part of its Awakenings programme, exploring the integration of digital systems and artificial intelligence into art and design practices. The event will take place on 17 October 2026 at the Hochhauser Auditorium within V&A South Kensington. The programme brings together artists Aziza Kadyri and Eunjo Lee in conversation with Contemporary Programme Curator Carrie Chan, examining how both artists draw inspiration from the museum collection and the role of technology in their work. The first session at 14.00 features Eunjo Lee discussing her work When the Void Gazes Back, which explores how artificial intelligence and data reshape spiritual awakenings and non-human consciousness through digitally sculpted films and sculptures. The second session at 15.00 features Aziza Kadyri, who will discuss her new commission Sender Unknown, an installation that reimagines textile traditions in Uzbekistan at the intersection of artificial intelligence, art, and craft in response to the museum's historic suzani collection. Kadyri examines how technologies that risk erasing histories can instead function as preservation tools. The event is free and open to the public, with advance booking required.

articles.originalTitle: In Conversation with Liu Jiakun, Dong Gong, and Luo Yujie: Small-Scale Timber Buildings—Why Build Them and How? - ArchDaily
articles.title: Small-Scale Timber Buildings and Architectural Design Competition
articles.excerpt: The second GoodOne Future Timber Architecture Design Competition opens registration to explore timber applications in urban regeneration and public spaces, featuring insights from lead judges.
articles.content: As timber architecture expands beyond traditional residential and rural settings into urban regeneration, commercial spaces, and public activities, the need for evolving new architecture grows. The second GoodOne Future Timber Architecture Design Competition aims to explore these questions. Jointly initiated by Hefei Jiuwucang Architectural Assembly Technology, Z/S Studio, and Luxelakes A8 Design Center, this year's competition adopts the theme A Fantastical Journey Within. It invites architects, designers, and creative practitioners worldwide and across disciplines to participate. Registration remains open until October 23, 2026, at 12:00 noon. The competition's three lead judges—Liu Jiakun, founder of Jiakun Architects; Dong Gong, founder of Vector Architects and foreign member of the French Academy of Architecture; and Luo Yujie, founder of LUO studio—shared their perspectives. Drawing on their respective design experiences, they discussed bamboo and timber, small-scale architecture, public space, construction principles, and long-term building operations.

articles.originalTitle: Sam Taylor-Johnson: The Self and the Portrait (Livestream) - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Sam Taylor-Johnson to Discuss Artistic Practice in V&A Online Conversation
articles.excerpt: Internationally acclaimed artist and filmmaker Sam Taylor-Johnson will discuss her new monograph and portraiture approach in an online conversation with journalist Tim Blanks.
articles.content: Artist and filmmaker Sam Taylor-Johnson will join journalist Tim Blanks in an online conversation hosted by the Victoria and Albert Museum. Scheduled for 12 November 2026 from 19.00 to 20.00, the talk will focus on her new monograph and her distinctive approach to portraiture. Tickets cost £8.00, with general booking opening on 19 October subject to availability. Spanning photography, installation and film, Taylor-Johnson has continuously explored boundaries between the private and public self, and she will discuss the evolution of her artistic vision. The event will be hosted on Zoom, with link distribution scheduled for the morning of the talk, and a recording will be provided for those unable to attend live. V&A members enjoy various benefits, and purchases from the museum shop support ongoing institution activities.

articles.originalTitle: Geometry that Generates Energy: The Solar Facade of Breidablikk Gården, Norway - ArchDaily
articles.title: Office Building in Norway Features Solar Energy Generating Facade
articles.excerpt: Breidablikk Gården in Haugesund, Norway, combines rooftop photovoltaics with an integrated solar facade developed alongside SolarLab, merging energy generation with the building envelope.
articles.content: Located in Haugesund, Norway, the Breidablikk Gården office building pairs rooftop photovoltaics with an integrated solar facade developed in collaboration with SolarLab. Designed by Asplan Viak, the east and west elevations feature angled panels oriented toward the south to boost energy yield while providing shading for the offices within. Addressing the region's low winter sun angles, the facade forms a repeated zigzag at each window, optimizing solar collection and reducing cooling requirements. The project achieves a peak photovoltaic capacity of 39.9 kWp, with the facade capable of generating approximately 100,000 kWh of electricity annually. Constructed using low-carbon wood and prefabricated wall modules, the building has attained BREEAM-NOR Excellent certification. Engineered for local rain and snow conditions, the ventilated rainscreen protects the primary structure while utilizing an iridescent surface treatment that interacts with changing daylight conditions in the urban setting.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026: performances, lectures, discussions, roundtables - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Biennale Arte 2026 Concludes at the Arsenale with a Public Program and Performances
articles.excerpt: The 61st International Art Exhibition, Biennale Arte 2026, concludes at the Arsenale from November 13 to 22 with a public program of performances, panels, and an assembly of artist collectives under Koyo Kouoh's curation 'In Minor Keys'.
articles.content: The 61st International Art Exhibition, Biennale Arte 2026, curated by Koyo Kouoh, concludes with a public program at the Arsenale in Venice from November 13 to 22. Spanning the final ten days of the exhibition 'In Minor Keys', the schedule features performances, lectures, debates, and roundtables, alongside an Assembly bringing together ten artist-led organizations and collectives. The program includes performances by artists such as Laurie Anderson, Ziad Antar, Tammy Nguyen, and Hagar Ophir. The gatherings provide spaces for artists, curators, and educators to share ideas regarding pedagogy, research, and community. Participating organizations include Denniston Hill, RAW Material Company, GAS Foundation, lugar a dudas, blaxTARLINES, Nairobi Contemporary Art Institute, Dar Jacir, Fresh Milk, Picha Collective, and Gudskul. The schedule also features lectures by guests such as Felwine Sarr and daily discussion assemblies.

articles.originalTitle: EXCLUSIVE: Dunhill Heads to Florence as Pitti Uomo’s Fall 2027 Guest Designer - WWD
articles.title: Dunhill Named Guest Designer for Upcoming Pitti Uomo in Florence
articles.excerpt: Richemont-owned luxury brand Dunhill will present its fall 2027 collection in Florence as the guest designer at the 111th edition of Pitti Immagine Uomo.
articles.content: London-based luxury menswear house Dunhill will serve as the guest designer at the 111th edition of Pitti Immagine Uomo in Florence. The brand has scheduled its fall 2027 collection presentation for Jan. 14, within the event running from Jan. 12 to 15. The collection draws inspiration from the historical relationship between English style and Florentine craftsmanship, emphasizing an Anglo-Florentine exchange of restraint and elegance. Dunhill creative director Simon Holloway stated that being invited to present at the forum is a significant honor for the label. Ivano Cauli, chief executive officer of Pitti Immagine, noted that the brand channels British sartorial tradition through a contemporary lens, while special events manager Francesca Tacconi highlighted its blend of refinement and adherence to tradition. Founded in London in 1893 and owned by Richemont, Dunhill offers a comprehensive wardrobe encompassing tailoring, outerwear, leather goods, and casualwear. Holloway, who assumed his creative post in 2023, previously worked with various Italian fashion houses and mills throughout his career.

articles.originalTitle: Boucheron Amps Up Its Spotlight in the U.S. with New Christie’s Exhibition - Robb Report
articles.title: Boucheron Mounts Comprehensive Heritage Exhibition in New York With Christie's
articles.excerpt: French jewelry house Boucheron is showcasing its historical heritage and craftsmanship at Christie's headquarters in New York. The ten-day exhibition brings together rare pieces spanning from the 19th century to the present day.
articles.content: French high jewelry maison Boucheron is presenting an extensive survey of exceptional jewels at Christie's headquarters in New York, featuring creations ranging from founder Frédéric Boucheron's era to earlier this year. Running from October 9 to 18, the exhibition titled "Boucheron: In Focus, a Monograph of a Visionary" highlights the maison's nearly 170-year history and its innovative design philosophy. Most items on display originate from the archive alongside loans from private collectors, organized under themes of architecture, nature, history, and innovation. According to CEO Hélène Poulit-Duquesne, the event aims to communicate the depth of the brand's heritage, encompassing both historical craftsmanship and modern innovation. Highlights include Lady Harcourt's 1924 diamond tiara and Mrs. Mackay's 1888 ruby and diamond collar necklace, both originating from the late 19th and early 20th centuries. In addition, dedicated zones showcase recent high jewelry collections titled Impermanence and Human Nature, featuring experimental materials and craft-intensive techniques overseen by creative director Claire Choisne. An accompanying catalog is also available for visitors to commemorate the ten-day cultural presentation.

articles.originalTitle: Art Basel announces 272 exhibitors and a reconfigured showfloor for its 2026 Miami Beach edition - Art Basel
articles.title: Art Basel Miami Beach Announces 272 Exhibitors and Reconfigured Layout for 2026
articles.excerpt: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from over 40 countries for its 2026 edition, featuring a substantially reconfigured showfloor and a more focused gallery lineup.
articles.content: Art Basel Miami Beach will bring together 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories for its upcoming edition, reaffirming its position as a major commercial moment in the U.S. art market. Taking place at the Miami Beach Convention Center from December 4 to 6, with VIP preview days on December 2 and 3, the fair introduces a substantially reconfigured layout based on feedback from exhibitors and the Selection Committee. The redesigned floor plan occupies approximately 12 percent less floor space, while the main Galleries sector features about 10 percent fewer exhibitors to create a more concentrated setting. The new layout organizes the space around four hospitality plazas instead of five, distributing blue-chip galleries throughout the showfloor to improve navigation and sightlines. The event spans multiple sectors including Galleries, Kabinett, Nova, Positions, and Survey, welcoming more than thirty first-time participating galleries mostly through its project-based sectors. Zero 10 returns with an expanded presentation dedicated to digital art. Public outdoor projects, partner awards, and institutional collaborations will accompany the main exhibition throughout the week.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Moldova Pavilion: HYBRIDREAMS – Imagining otherwise in times of crisis - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Roundtable on Crises and the Future Held at the Moldova Pavilion in the Venice Biennale
articles.excerpt: The Moldova Pavilion at the Venice Biennale is hosting an open panel addressing how war and current crises alter projections of the future.
articles.content: Drawing upon the project marking the Republic of Moldova’s inaugural official participation in the International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia, a roundtable discussion titled HYBRIDREAMS – Imagining otherwise in times of crisis is taking place on 16 October at the Chiesa dei Santi Geremia e Lucia in Venice. The event explores how war and contemporary crises are reshaping future projections. Organized in collaboration with the Europe Cultural Foundation and the European Council on Foreign Relations, the programme opens with a tour led by church administrator Don Gianmatteo Caputo. The discussion expands from Moldova's geopolitical realities to examine how political thought, cultural practice, and artistic imagination respond to conflict. Speakers include Nicu Popescu, André Wilkens, and Silvia Eiblmayr, with moderation by curator Adelina Luft. The public event is hosted at the Moldova Pavilion venue.

articles.originalTitle: ENR 2026 Top 100 Green Design Firms and Contractors: Green Building Market Deepens - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Green Building Market Deepens While Navigating Cost and Policy Challenges
articles.excerpt: While sustainable design and contracting revenues are on the rise, industry stakeholders are grappling with challenges such as federal incentive rollbacks, rising costs, and data gaps.
articles.content: Last year, the revenue of the top 100 green design firms increased by 17.1% to $11.8 billion, while international green design revenue rose 18.3% to $2.15 billion. The revenue of the top 100 green contractors also increased by 5.9% to $101.9 billion. While growth varied across markets, the largest increases were observed in industrial processes, hotels, and health care. However, industry experts point out that the rollback of federal sustainability incentives has created a ripple effect on project costs. Jill Kurtz from Stantec notes that many projects face uncertainties regarding real-world performance, emphasizing that decisions should be grounded in building science and operational data rather than certifications alone. Renée Azerbegi of Mead & Hunt states that shifting policy priorities and reduced incentive programs have generated funding uncertainty. Anica Landreneau from HOK reported that clients are increasingly concerned about grid reliability and energy resilience. Contractors suggest that bringing designers and trade partners together early on is critical in translating sustainability goals into practical decisions.

articles.originalTitle: Ca’ Querini ai Greci - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Historic Ca’ Querini ai Greci Exhibition and Event Space Presented in Venice
articles.excerpt: Located close to San Marco, the historic Ca’ Querini ai Greci building offers dedicated halls and water access for exhibitions, conferences, and cocktails.
articles.content: Situated a short distance from San Marco, the historic Ca’ Querini ai Greci building in Venice features suitable infrastructure for art exhibitions, conferences, and cocktail receptions. The exhibition space on the first floor comprises a central hall of approximately 60 square meters and five large rooms overlooking the Rio dei Greci. The venue provides an exclusive ground-floor entrance and private water access from the canal for loading and unloading artworks. Public transport connections include Actv vaporetto lines stopping at Pietà and San Zaccaria. Available facilities at the Castello address include private water access, bathroom fixtures, lighting, heating, a back terrace, a balcony facing Rio dei Greci, and wi-fi connectivity. Contact details for the location are managed by delegate Antonella Stefani.
